text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Federation Council, the upper chamber of Russian parliament, has approved a new tax on buying foreign currency. President Boris Yeltsin is likely to sign this law soon.
- President Yeltsin had to step in to settle a long-running conflict over Tyumen Oil Company.
- The government has apparently started its programme of reforms of natural monopolies by changing the way RAO UES of Russia, the country's energy monopoly, functions.
- The government, in an effort to introduce a new tax code early next year, has started work on specific regulations before the code is approved by parliament.
- The governors of three regions in Russia's Far East have signed a cooperation agreement which should demonstrate to Moscow their drive for economic independence.
- Moscow is keen to improve relations with Baku and is likely to make some political concessions to get oil running from Azerbaijan through Russian territory.
- UNEXIM Bank's failure to get its people promoted to the board of directors of gas giant Gazprom may be seen as a sign that this bank is losing some of its power.
- President Yeltsin's involvement in resolving the Tyumen Oil Company conflict demonstrates that no one was really interested in the Nizhnevartovskneftegaz company going bankrupt.
- Talks between the Russian and Azeri presidents have moved forward a number of acute problems in relations.
- Russian businessmen are irritated by the Western media, which apparently creates a negative image of Russia.
- Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin is in perfect working form after taking a holiday.

- Talk about the possible resignation of Sergei Belyayev as head of Our Home is Russia's parliamentary group, and the scandal around fellow party member Lev Rokhlin, prove that the pro-government faction is far from united.
- The federal centre continues to share power with the regions. This is the only way to give regions equal opportunities for economic development.
